setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Scarlet solo has intense guitar peaks; the Scarlet>Fire pairing closes the first set; Scarlet>Fire was very new at this show, according to the reviewer [9][15]
- **Samson and Delilah** (2 reviews): Reviewer, who attended, rates this the best Samson and Delilah they have ever heard; Reviewer found the Samson and Delilah especially smoking [6][8]
- **Estimated Prophet** (2 reviews): Hearing Estimated Prophet on that radio tape while driving through Death Valley won the reviewer over to the band; Estimated Prophet was very new at this show, and the band sounded tight [13][15]
- **Jack-A-Roe** (1 review): First time played; slower than later versions but still good [9]
- **Fire on the Mountain** (1 review): Jerry tears up every lead in Fire, one with an octave effect [9]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer finds The Other One devastatingly powerful, loud enough to make them want to hide [10]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: Jack-A-Roe [16]

## The recordings

- **gd77-05-13.sbd.miller.9393.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 154 min; rated 4.54/5 by 61 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this the pre-FM tape, cleaner than the radio copy, with a bad flaw late in Goin' Down the Road [6]
- **gd1977-05-13.sbd.ashley.14942.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 154 min; rated 4.19/5 by 26 [2]. Said about its sound: Post-drums disc was de-emphasised to offset PCM emphasis; a right-channel dropout on D3t05 was patched from the left, making it mono [2]
- **gd1977-05-13.sbd.unknown.6690.sbeok.shnf**: pre-FM broadcast master; 19 songs; 161 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer was in the audience and says the band seemed lit up [6]
- The show was simulcast on radio, and the reviewer taped it that night; it was their first Dead show [15]
- Chicago radio station WXRT hosted the shows, and a poster print was likely overseen by them [19]
- The show was officially released in the May 1977 box set [20]
- May 8 is the famous peak of the run; this show sits on its slope alongside others [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-05-13.sbd.miller.9393.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: A friend taped the show live off Chicago radio; the reviewer later also heard this soundboard version; Soundboard to reel to DAT to CD, then Sonic Solutions to CD; post-drums section came via a different DAT path; seeded by Charlie Miller [1][13]
- **gd1977-05-13.sbd.ashley.14942.shnf**: transferred by Jay Ashley; source: SBD>>MR>>Dat>>CDA>>SS>>CDA>>SHN>>DAW(Bertha)>>CDA [2]. Also: Remastered on 10/5/2002 by an archive.org user on a dual-DAW named Bertha; post-drums disc is thought to be pre-FM via DAT [2]
- **gd1977-05-13.sbd.unknown.6690.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by unknown; source: Pre-FM > Master Reel > DAT > CD [3]
